source_inspections.origin_group: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Indiana
source_inspections.evidence_extract: The public docket for James v. English, No. 3:26-cv-01225, records an August 19 federal habeas petition by Phillip Michael Thomas James, also identified as Felibi Biladi Siagha-Coke. The docket lists sealed supporting exhibits including a birth certificate, State Department passport-revocation letter, Florida court records, communications with Jamaican authorities and medical reports. The filing and exhibit descriptions establish the pending challenge and evidence submitted, not the truth of every disputed assertion.
source_inspections.hash_scope: SHA-256 of the exact normalized evidence extract retained here, not a claim of hashing the complete source document.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: Associated Press reported at 7:08 UTC that ICE has detained James since January 5 while seeking removal to Jamaica. AP independently obtained a 1988 Florida paternity record matching the filed birth certificate, reported prior U.S. passports and citizenship entries in criminal records, and described medical reports attributing his Jamaican-birth claims to paranoid schizophrenia. DHS alleged the birth certificate was fraudulent but supplied no evidence to AP, denied detaining U.S. citizens and said removal proceedings provide due process. Citizenship, habeas relief and the immigration appeal remained unresolved.
